name: Double front-rack squat
explain: Hold two bells at your shoulders, elbows tucked, and squat down until your hips are below your knees, then stand tall.

name: Goblet squat
explain: Hold one bell at your chest by the horns and squat between your knees, chest up, then drive back up.
source: The Complete Guide to Kettlebells for Firefighters

name: Bulgarian split squat (goblet)
explain: Back foot on a bench, bell at your chest, lower straight down on the front leg until the back knee nearly touches, then stand.

name: Cossack squat
explain: Wide stance, shift your hips down over one leg while the other stays straight with toes up, then switch sides.

name: Tempo goblet squat (4-1-1)
explain: A goblet squat taking 4 seconds down, 1 second pause, 1 second up. App swap for EH's stability-ball hack squat.

name: Zombie squat
explain: Arms held straight out in front (or bell at the chest) and squat with an upright torso; trains a strong, balanced squat.

name: Single front-rack squat
explain: One bell racked at one shoulder; squat while resisting the lean to that side, then switch.
source: Do a Station Workout WITH ME

name: Heels-elevated squat
explain: Heels on a plate or board, squat straight down letting the knees travel forward. Deep, knee-friendly quad work.

name: Sumo squat
explain: Wide stance, toes out, bell hanging between your legs; sit straight down and stand up squeezing the glutes.
source: Pass the CPAT on Your First Try

name: B-stance squat
explain: One foot slightly back on its toes as a kickstand; squat with most of your weight on the front leg.
source: Do a Station Workout WITH ME

name: Spanish squat
explain: Band behind your knees anchored in front, sit back into a squat with shins vertical and hold. Builds knee strength with little pain.
source: Stop Training Legs Like A Bodybuilder (short)

name: Split-stance iso hold
explain: Hold the bottom of a split squat without moving for 30-45 seconds; isometrics strengthen tendons around the knee.
source: Stop Training Legs Like A Bodybuilder (short)

name: Reverse lunge
explain: Step one foot back and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees, then push through the front foot to stand.
source: Train Like a Firefighter at Home With Just ONE Kettlebell

name: Forward lunge
explain: Step forward, lower until the back knee nearly touches, then push back to the start.
source: Train Like a Firefighter at Home With Just ONE Kettlebell

name: Reverse suitcase lunge
explain: Hold a weight at your side like a suitcase and reverse lunge without leaning toward it.
source: Get Fit Like a FIREFIGHTER With These 6 MUST KNOW Exercises

name: Front-foot-elevated reverse lunge
explain: Front foot on a small plate or step, step back into a lunge. The elevation gives a deeper, knee-friendlier range.
source: Stop Training Legs Like A Bodybuilder (short)

name: Overhead reverse lunge
explain: Lock a bell overhead and reverse lunge while keeping the arm straight and ribs down.

name: Side lunge
explain: Step wide to one side, sit your hips back over that foot, then push back to center.
source: Tight Hips? Try This Kettlebell Exercise (short)

name: Squat to halo
explain: Hold a bell by the horns, squat, stand, then circle it around your head once. Mobility under load.

name: Barbell back squat
explain: Bar on your upper back, squat to depth with a braced core, then stand. Standard lift exception.

name: Barbell front squat
explain: Bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high, squat to depth staying upright. Standard lift exception.

name: Trap bar deadlift
explain: Stand inside a trap bar, hinge and grip the handles, brace, and stand up driving through the floor.

name: Barbell deadlift
explain: Bar over mid-foot, hinge and grip, flat back, stand by pushing the floor away. Standard lift exception.

name: KB/DB deadlift
explain: Weight between your feet, push your hips back with a flat back, grab it, and stand tall.
source: Tight Hips? Try This Kettlebell Exercise (short)

name: B-stance RDL
explain: Back foot on its toes as a kickstand, push your hips back on the front leg with a soft knee and flat back, then stand.

name: Single-leg RDL
explain: Balance on one leg and hinge forward as the other leg reaches back, then return tall.
source: Get MORE Gains in LESS Time (KB supersets)

name: Incline deadlift
explain: A deadlift variation from the pull-focused workout; hinge with flat back and stand fully.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Kettlebell swing (Russian)
explain: Hike the bell back between your legs and snap your hips forward so it floats to chest height.

name: American swing
explain: A swing that continues to overhead with arms straight; finish with the bell stacked above you.

name: Single-arm KB swing
explain: The swing with one hand; resist your torso twisting.
source: This Viral Workout is PERFECT for Firefighters

name: Kickstand swing
explain: Swing with one foot back as a kickstand to load one hip more.
source: Get MORE Gains in LESS Time (KB supersets)

name: Kettlebell clean
explain: Hike the bell back and pop the hips to bring it to the rack at your shoulder, elbow tucked.
source: The Complete Guide to Kettlebells for Firefighters

name: Tactical clean
explain: A two-hand-on-horns style clean to the chest; snap the hips and catch softly.

name: Kettlebell snatch
explain: One continuous swing to overhead, punching through at the top so the bell lands softly.
source: The Complete Guide to Kettlebells for Firefighters

name: Tactical snatch
explain: Explosive hip drive bringing the bell overhead in one motion.

name: Kettlebell windmill
explain: Bell locked overhead, push your hip out and slide the free hand down your leg while watching the bell.

name: Hamstring eccentric sliders
explain: In a bridge with heels on sliders or a towel, slowly slide your feet out in small steps, then reset.
source: Get MORE Gains in LESS Time (KB supersets)

name: Glute bridge (hold)
explain: On your back, feet planted, squeeze your glutes to lift your hips and hold.

name: Kettlebell push-up
explain: Push-up with hands on bell handles for a deeper range and neutral wrists.

name: Push-up
explain: Rigid plank, lower your chest to just above the floor, then press up.

name: Hand-release push-up
explain: Lower all the way to the floor, lift your hands an inch, then press back up. Forces full depth.

name: Deficit push-up
explain: Hands on handles or plates so your chest drops below hand level for extra range.

name: Glute bridge floor press
explain: On your back with hips up in a bridge, press one or two bells from your chest.

name: Rotational overhead press
explain: Press the bell overhead while rotating your torso away from it, pivoting the back foot.

name: KB clean to press
explain: Clean the bell to your shoulder, then press it overhead. Every rep starts from the ground.

name: Z press
explain: Sit on the floor legs straight and press overhead with no back support. Exposes weak cores fast.

name: KB push press
explain: Small dip of the knees, then drive up and use that pop to press the bell overhead.
source: Get MORE Gains in LESS Time (KB supersets)

name: Tall-kneeling push press
explain: Kneel tall, snap your hips forward, and use that pop to drive the bell overhead.

name: Half-kneeling press
explain: One knee down, press the bell overhead on the same side as the down knee; anti-rotation.
source: 6 Simple Exercises That Build Firefighter Strength FAST

name: Half-kneeling bottoms-up KB press
explain: Hold the bell upside down by the handle and press it overhead; great for shoulder health.
source: The Best Exercise To Reduce Shoulder Pain (short)

name: Single-arm overhead press
explain: Bell racked at the shoulder, brace and press straight overhead.
source: This Viral Workout is PERFECT for Firefighters

name: Alternating overhead press
explain: Two bells at your shoulders, press one up at a time.
source: Do a Station Workout WITH ME

name: Viper press
explain: A press variation from EH's push day.

name: Waiter clean to waiter press
explain: Clean the bell into a waiter hold (flat palm under it) and press it overhead.

name: Hollow press
explain: Lie in a hollow hold and press a bell up with one arm without losing the shape.

name: Neutral-grip DB press
explain: Press dumbbells with palms facing each other; easier on the shoulders.
source: The Best Exercise To Reduce Shoulder Pain (short)

name: Barbell bench press
explain: Lie on a bench and press the bar from your chest. Standard lift exception.

name: Barbell push press
explain: Dip and drive to press the bar overhead. Standard lift exception.

name: Pull-ups
explain: Hang from a bar and pull your chest up toward it. Band-assist if needed.

name: Eccentric pull-up
explain: Jump or step to the top and lower yourself for 5 seconds.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Lat pulldown
explain: Pull the bar to your upper chest with elbows driving down.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Alternating gorilla row
explain: Wide hinge with two bells on the floor; row one at a time while the other pushes into the floor.

name: Locomotive row
explain: Hinged with a bell in each hand, row them alternately like train pistons.

name: Renegade row
explain: In a plank on two bells, row one to your hip without your hips twisting.

name: Renegade row with push-up
explain: Push-up on the bells, then a row on each side.
source: This Viral Workout is PERFECT for Firefighters

name: Bird dog row
explain: On hands and knees, extend the opposite leg back and row the bell to your ribs without tipping.
source: Exercises I STOPPED Doing as a Firefighter

name: Bench-supported row
explain: One hand and knee on a bench, flat back, row the weight to your hip.
source: If I Could Only Do 6 Exercises as a Firefighter

name: Plank row
explain: In a high plank with one hand on a bell, row it up without twisting.
source: Exercises I STOPPED Doing as a Firefighter

name: Single-arm row
explain: Hinge with a hand braced, row the bell to your hip.
source: The Complete Guide to Kettlebells for Firefighters

name: Ballistic row
explain: An explosive row from the hang driven by the hips and back.
source: Pass the CPAT on Your First Try

name: KB high pull
explain: Swing-style hip snap pulling the bell to chest height with elbows high.

name: KB curl to pullover
explain: Lying on your back, curl the bell to your chest, then take it overhead in a pullover.

name: Horn curl
explain: Hold the bell by the horns and curl it to your chin.

name: Concentration curl
explain: Seated, elbow on your inner thigh, curl slowly.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Hollow hold
explain: Low back pressed to the floor, lift shoulders and legs a few inches and hold.

name: Bear plank
explain: On hands and toes, knees hovering an inch off the floor; hold rock solid.

name: Bear plank KB drag
explain: In a bear plank, reach under and drag the bell across to the other side.

name: North-south KB drag
explain: In a plank, drag the bell forward and back without your hips moving.
source: The Only 6 Core Exercises Firefighters Need

name: Kettlebell chop
explain: Diagonal chop from high to low across your body, rotating through hips and trunk.

name: Half-kneeling cable chop
explain: Half-kneeling, pull a cable or band diagonally across your body.

name: Kettlebell uppercut
explain: Drive a bell up and across like an uppercut using hip rotation.

name: KB halo with rotation
explain: Circle the bell around your head and add a trunk turn.

name: Around the world with rotation
explain: Pass the bell around your body hand to hand, adding rotation.

name: Bird dog
explain: On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg, pause, return.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Side plank
explain: On one forearm, body straight, hips high; hold.
source: MY WORKOUT After a Firefighter Shift (Pull Focused)

name: Banded/suitcase march
explain: Weight in one hand, march slowly lifting knees without leaning.
source: If I Could Only Do 6 Exercises as a Firefighter

name: Goblet march
explain: Hold a bell at your chest and march in place slowly.
source: Get MORE Gains in LESS Time (KB supersets)

name: Single overhead march
explain: Lock a bell overhead and march in place.

name: Split-stance KB exchange
explain: In a split stance, pass the bell hand to hand under the front leg.

name: Gun slingers
explain: Shoulder rotation drill with a light bell from EH's shoulder short.
source: The Best Exercise To Reduce Shoulder Pain (short)

name: Farmer's walk
explain: Heavy weight in each hand, walk tall for distance.

name: Suitcase carry
explain: Weight in one hand only; walk without leaning.

name: Equipment carry
explain: Carry awkward gear or a heavy bell for distance like on the job.
source: Pass the CPAT on Your First Try

name: Hose drag
explain: Drag a charged line or sled backward or forward.
source: Pass the CPAT on Your First Try

name: Victim drag
explain: Drag a dummy or heavy bag backward for distance.
source: Pass the CPAT on Your First Try

name: Burpee
explain: Squat down, jump feet back, chest to floor, jump feet in, jump up.
source: Stop Feeling Out of Breath on Duty (Firefighter HIIT)

name: Pop squat / jump squat
explain: Squat and explode into a jump, land softly.
source: Stop Feeling Out of Breath on Duty (Firefighter HIIT)

name: Plyometric lunge
explain: Jump and switch legs in a lunge.
source: Stop Feeling Out of Breath on Duty (Firefighter HIIT)

name: Ball slams
explain: Lift a slam ball overhead and throw it down hard.
source: Every Firefighter Should Train in FULL GEAR

name: Battle rope
explain: Fast alternating waves with the rope.
source: Every Firefighter Should Train in FULL GEAR

name: Tire step-up
explain: Alternate stepping up onto a tire.
source: Every Firefighter Should Train in FULL GEAR

name: SkiErg
explain: Pull the handles down driving from hips and lats.

name: Rower
explain: Legs, then hips, then arms; reverse on the return.

name: StairMaster
explain: Steady stair climbing.

name: Run (outdoors)
explain: Easy-to-hard running outside depending on the day.

name: Brisk (uphill) walk
explain: Fast walk, hills if available; aerobic base work.
source: The FASTEST Way to Improve Cardio

name: Ruck
explain: Walk with a loaded pack at conversational pace.
source: The FASTEST Way to Improve Cardio

name: 90/90 hip rotations
explain: Sit with both knees at 90 degrees and rotate them side to side without your hands.
source: Burn 2X the Calories in HALF the Time (KB EMOM)

name: Banded lateral / monster walk
explain: Band around the legs, quarter squat, step sideways then diagonally.
source: Burn 2X the Calories in HALF the Time (KB EMOM)

name: Couch stretch
explain: Back knee on a pad, shin up a couch, front foot planted, squeeze the glute. Opens quads and hip flexors.

name: Cat cow
explain: On hands and knees, alternate arching and rounding the back slowly.

name: Thread the needle
explain: On hands and knees, slide one arm under your body and rotate.

name: Deep squat rock
explain: Sit in a deep squat and rock gently side to side to open the ankles.

name: Foam roller T-spine extensions
explain: Roller under your upper back, extend over it, 3 breaths per segment.

name: Banded hip swivel
explain: Band high in the groin, walk out for tension and swivel the hip.

name: Banded half-kneeling hip flexor
explain: Half-kneeling with band tension on the hip; push hips forward gently.

name: Banded world's greatest stretch
explain: Lunge, hand down, rotate the other arm to the ceiling.
